slot.brief: Ice at 0°C mixed with water at higher temperature; track latent heat plus sensible heat exchange to find final temperature or unmelted ice mass.

stem: 40 g of ice at 0 deg C is mixed with 120 g of water at 20 deg C in an insulated container. Take specific heat of water = 1 cal g^-1 deg C^-1 and latent heat of fusion of ice = 80 cal g^-1. The mass of ice that remains when thermal equilibrium is reached is:

verdicts.working: Water cools to 0°C, releasing 120 × 20 = 2400 cal. This melts 2400/80 = 30 g of ice, leaving 40 − 30 = 10 g.

working:
Heat released by water cooling to 0 deg C = 120 * 1 * 20 = 2400 cal. Heat required to melt all 40 g ice = 40 * 80 = 3200 cal. Since 2400 cal < 3200 cal, final temperature is 0 deg C and some ice remains. Mass of ice melted = 2400 / 80 = 30 g. Mass remaining = 40 - 30 = 10 g. Thus option B.

Independent check: Water cools to 0°C, releasing 120 × 20 = 2400 cal. This melts 2400/80 = 30 g of ice, leaving 40 − 30 = 10 g.
solution:
Heat released by water cooling to $0^\circ\mathrm C$ is $Q=120(1)(20)=2400\,\mathrm{cal}$, less than the $3200\,\mathrm{cal}$ needed to melt all the ice.
$$m_{\text{melted}}=\frac{2400}{80}=30\,\mathrm g,\qquad m_{\text{remaining}}=40-30=10\,\mathrm g$$
